title: Deep Chand v. State of U.P.

content.caseIdentity: Deep Chand v. State of U.P., AIR 1959 SC 648
content.facts: The appellants were permit-holders operating stage-carriage buses on routes in Uttar Pradesh. They challenged the Uttar Pradesh Transport Service (Development) Act, 1955, and the State's transport-nationalisation scheme and notifications. After the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 1956 introduced a central framework for transport nationalisation, the appellants also raised questions of repugnancy under Article 254 and the continuing effect of the State scheme.
questionsBeforeCourt: Whether the Uttar Pradesh Transport Service (Development) Act, 1955 became wholly void or inoperative because of the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 1956
Whether the State transport-nationalisation scheme was affected by repugnancy under Article 254
Whether the constitutional validity of the State enactment and scheme was affected by the constitutional changes concerning Article 31
content.ratioDecidendi: A later central enactment does not automatically extinguish an earlier State law and an already-framed scheme; repugnancy under Article 254 must be determined by comparing the laws and the field they occupy. The judgment also treated the constitutional validity of a law according to the constitutional limitations applicable when it was enacted, subject to subsequent changes that remove or alter the relevant limitation.
content.holding: Post-Constitution laws violating Article 13(2) are still-born and void ab initio; the Doctrine of Eclipse does not apply to revive them against citizens.
content.relevance: Established important principles on repugnancy, Article 254, and the temporal operation of constitutional limitations, and is also cited in the development of the doctrine concerning post-Constitution unconstitutional laws.
